what: Data upgrades run 2026-10-09: each dataset built by one agent and independently re-derived by a second (skeptic) agent. Builder summaries are omitted; this file keeps the verifier checks and problems. How each problem was handled is in handoff_resolution.

handoff_resolution.occupancy_kh: Rebuilt with owners/occupancy_kh.py (duplicate Kauai record dropped, X999 label fixed, reconciliation note corrected); ordinance citation, tier and exempt-parcel caveats added to sources/occupancy_kh.json notes. Unflagged sub-counts under 20 remain in the detail and are not shown in the report.
handoff_resolution.visitors_2025: JSON was correct; the report uses its 2025 values (Table 56). Summary rounding/wording errors did not reach the report.
handoff_resolution.official_sources: Report citation dates corrected (why/build_why.py fix_date). IRS provenance note recorded; no numbers changed.
handoff_resolution.market_oct: Kauai and Hawaii Island September board figures added from the verifier; mislabelled Aug-edition YTD key renamed; Hawaii Island Aug YTD attribution noted. September figures shown in #now with sources; DBEDT remains canonical for the monthly series.

problems: Minor double count: one Kauai class-11 parcel is in the layer twice (same PARID and values), so the Kauai universe should be 27,097 (class 11 = 1,119, which matches the official count). Headline shares change by less than 0.01 point.

The reconciliation note's line 'The State summary counts taxable records' is not supported. Kauai's taxable class-8 count (11,156) and total class-8 count (11,702) both differ from the official 11,550, and other classes don't line up either. Say instead that the cause of the small differences is unknown.

The gap is out of date: kauai.gov is reachable now. The Bill 2944 PDF the builder logged as HTTP 403 returned 200 on re-check. Its text (Kauai County Code 5A-9.1) confirms the class decoding and the 3% owner-occupied assessment cap, which supports reading MODTOT as market value. That ordinance should be cited as the official class definition. Note that the layer's codes 10 and 11 differ from the ordinance's list numbers (9) and (10); the labels match.

Some small cells are not flagged: Hawaii North Hilo multi-unit TMKs (6, in two places), the 1-19 improved / with-exemption sub-counts in five districts, Kauai fully-exempt federal 9, and 14 owner_type_mix counts of 1-19 (e.g. county 1, state 1).

Mislabel: the Hawaii bottom-5 NHoodCode X999 is labelled 'North Kona CCD (mostly outside Census-designated places)'. Only 23.7% of its parcels are outside a CDP, and it spans several districts (40.9% North Kona), so it is a catch-all code. It is not in the top 15.

Caveat to add: Hawaii County tiers use whole-TMK summed values. 343 owner-occupied TMKs have exemptions above $300K (likely two or more homes on one lot), so a few multi-home lots may sit in higher tiers. The layer also does not say whether PITT 500 LandValue is agricultural-use or market value.

The task asked for assessed-value tiers, but the Kauai $3M+ headline (72.8% of 1,356) uses MODTOT, an undocumented field read as market value. On assessed value (ASSDTOT) the figure is 85.6% of 1,130. Both tables are in the file and the inference is disclosed; make sure the report wording says 'market value'.

The 3,822 fully exempt Hawaii parcels left out are described as 'mostly DHHL, government and nonprofit'. A County BigstOwner aggregate shows DHHL 1,908, other State 200, County 110, Federal 14 (58% government in total) and 'other' 1,568 (41%). The nonprofit share of 'other' cannot be checked.
